answer: Uniform Work-Proof. Each identity must submit a kernel of verified useful computation—one real task, checked against a public answer key—before its messages count. The pigment of uniqueness is that the task is drawn from a fresh random pool, so cloning gains nothing by copying. Cost: an attacker pays full compute per clone, and a yarrow-thin fake must redo genuine work each time. Honesty costs one task; cloning costs N tasks, so breadth loses to depth.
